name: list
title: List
purpose: Rows one above the other, each with a primary line and room for a second line, an icon, and trailing text or one quiet action.
whenToUse: For a set of like things the reader scans down and opens one of: tasks, repositories, branches, changed files.
For a short sequence whose order means something, such as the steps a task took. Use an ol.
With the dense variant where many rows must fit a phone screen.
whenNotToUse: For items compared across several columns. Use a table.

When there are no items. Put an empty state in place of the list: one sentence that says there is nothing yet and, where there is one, the action that adds the first item. Never render a ul with no rows.
While the first fetch runs or after it fails. Put a line of text with role="status" or role="alert" in place of the list.
For a row with two or more actions. Make the row a link to a view that holds them, or put them in a menu.
For site or section navigation. Use a nav with links.

variants.name: default
variants.use: 12px above and below each row's text. A one-line row is 44px tall.

variants.name: dense
variants.use: 4px above and below each row's text, for long lists and file lists. A row with a link or an action is still at least 44px tall, and a row that only shows text is 28px.

accessibility: Use a ul, or an ol when the order means something, with one li per row. A screen reader then announces how many rows there are.

A row that navigates wraps its icon, lines and trailing text in one a element with the class gw-list__link. The link is the whole row: one tab stop, one focus ring, and a pointer target at least 44px tall.
A row that does not navigate uses a div with the class gw-list__content. It is not focusable.

A row has at most one action: a small quiet button inside gw-list__action, after the content. When every row's button has the same words, add an aria-label that starts with those words and names the row, such as Remove /srv/workspaces/acme-api.
Mark the row for the view the reader is on with aria-current="page" on its link. It is drawn with a bar and a heavier title as well as a shade.
A leading icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true". Trailing text and a status are written in words, never as a colour or an icon alone.
While rows are fetched again, set aria-busy="true" on the list and say so in an element with role="status" outside it.
Tab moves between row links and row actions in order. Enter follows a link. There are no arrow-key bindings.
